metadata.note: The New London Northern -- eastern Connecticut's north-south main line, from New London up the Thames past Norwich to Willimantic, then across Massachusetts through Palmer and Amherst to Millers Falls and Brattleboro, Vermont. It began as the New London, Willimantic and Palmer Railroad, open in stages through 1849 and 1850; the New London Northern took its property on 30 March 1861 and pushed north, buying the Amherst, Belchertown and Palmer in 1864, reaching Millers Falls on 8 October 1866 and buying the last 21 miles to Brattleboro from the Vermont and Massachusetts on 1 May 1880 -- 125.18 miles in final form. The Central Vermont leased it from 25 June 1873 and worked it for the rest of its passenger life, which ended in 1966. Carried as five features so that both the change of operator and the growth of the line are visible: the drawn extent stops at Palmer until 1866, at Millers Falls until 1880, and reaches Brattleboro only after that. It meets the Norwich and Worcester (norwich_worcester_railroad.geojson) at Norwich, the two lines together making Norwich a junction between Worcester and the Sound.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_London_Northern_Railroad and https://nashuacitystation.org/history/new-london-northern-railroad-company/ (New London, Willimantic and Palmer opened Norwich-Willimantic September 1849, Norwich-New London the next month, Willimantic-Palmer by March 1850; New London Northern incorporated 1859 and 1860 in Connecticut and Massachusetts, acquired the NLW&P property 30 March 1861; acquired the Amherst, Belchertown and Palmer 1 March 1864; completed 14.5 miles Amherst to Millers Falls 8 October 1866; acquired the 21 miles Millers Falls to Brattleboro from the Vermont and Massachusetts 1 May 1880; final form 125.18 miles New London to Brattleboro; leased to and operated by the Central Vermont Railroad from 25 June 1873)

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montrealer_(train) and https://www.american-rails.com/vermont.html (the Montrealer ran northbound and the Washingtonian southbound from 1924; Central Vermont passenger service terminated in 1966, the trains discontinued that September; Amtrak revived the Montrealer 1972-1995 and the Vermonter followed)
metadata.not_yet_sourced: All headways are estimated. The 1849 Norwich - Willimantic and Norwich - New London months are not drawn as their own era; the first feature starts in 1850 when the full New London - Palmer extent was open. Whether local passenger service on the Connecticut end outlasted or fell short of the 1966 through-train discontinuance was not established, so 1966 is used for the whole line.

segments.note: Opened in stages: Norwich to Willimantic in September 1849, Norwich to New London the next month, and Willimantic to Palmer, Massachusetts by March 1850. The feature starts at 1850 because that is when the drawn New London - Palmer extent was complete; the 1849 Norwich - Willimantic months are not drawn separately. Frequency estimated, unsourced.

The through Washington - Montreal sleeper era: the Montrealer northbound and the Washingtonian southbound ran from 1924, over this line north from New London. Central Vermont passenger service ended in 1966, the Montrealer and Washingtonian being discontinued that September. Amtrak revived the Montrealer in 1972 and the Vermonter succeeded it in 1995, but the modern train reaches Vermont by a different southern route and since 2014 runs via Northampton -- see montrealer.geojson and amtrak.geojson, both of which carry the modern alignment, not this one. Frequency estimated, unsourced.
